categories.main_business_segments: LEC, INC. operates primarily in the planning, manufacturing, and sales of daily necessities, including household goods, cleaning and hygiene consumables, and related products. The company reports a single business segment: 'Daily Necessities and Apparel Business.'
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company emphasizes rapid product planning and development, leveraging accumulated ideas and technologies to create high value-added, innovative, and cost-effective products. Manufacturing is conducted both in-house and through partner factories, with a focus on productivity, quality improvement, and efficient production systems, including the use of molds and automation.
categories.primary_customers_markets: LEC serves a wide range of consumers through major retail channels, with key customers including large discount and 100-yen shop chains such as Daiso and Seria, which together account for over 40% of sales. The company also targets the broader mass retail and drugstore markets, as well as character goods and OEM/ODM clients.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s main market is Japan, which accounts for over 90% of sales. It also operates manufacturing and sales subsidiaries in China, Thailand, Vietnam, and the United States, with production bases and logistics facilities in both Japan and Asia.
categories.supply_chain_position: LEC operates primarily as a midstream and downstream player, handling product planning, manufacturing (both in-house and outsourced), and direct sales to retailers and wholesalers. The company also manages logistics and distribution to its retail partners.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include strengthening new product development, expanding character-licensed product lines, and pursuing M&A for growth. The company invests in R&D to quickly respond to diverse consumer needs, enhance product value, and develop environmentally conscious products. There is also a focus on operational efficiency, cost control, and sustainability initiatives aligned with SDGs.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated mainly through the sale of physical products to retailers and wholesalers, with additional income from licensing character brands and, recently, from the acquisition of beverage brands. Sales are recognized upon delivery or shipment to customers.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: LEC competes with other major Japanese daily goods manufacturers and suppliers, such as Lion, Kao, and Unicharm, as well as with private label and OEM/ODM providers. The company positions itself as a leading, innovative, and consumer-focused manufacturer with strong capabilities in rapid product development and character goods.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated net sales reached 66.3 billion yen, with operating profit of 2.7 billion yen and net profit attributable to parent company shareholders of 1.7 billion yen. The company has shown steady sales growth (9.1% YoY), with a recent recovery in profitability after a period of margin pressure. Total assets are approximately 89.4 billion yen, and the company employs around 924 people on a consolidated basis.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: LEC differentiates itself through rapid, idea-driven product development, high cost-performance, and the ability to quickly respond to changing consumer needs. The company emphasizes unique, value-added products, including character-branded goods, and aims to deliver products that 'move' and satisfy customers, supported by strong R&D and a flexible, customer-oriented approach.
